# Printing Only the Required Number of Digits

#### Course: Learn C Programming

## Printing Only the Required Number of Digits

If we have a double variable PI assigned a value of 3.1415 and we print it, we'll get 3.141500 as the output.

This is because printf() prints 6 digits after the decimal point by default.

To restrict printf() to print 2 digits after the decimal point, we can use the format specifier %.2lf.

Similarly, we can use %.3lf, %.4lf, and so on to print 3, 4 and more digits respectively.

Let's see how we can improve our previous program to print exactly four digits of our double variable.

```c
1#include <stdio.h>
2
3int main() {
4
5    // Initialize a double variable
6    double PI = 3.1415;
7    
8     // Print six digits after the decimal point
9     printf("%lf", PI);
10
11    // Print a space
12    printf(" ");
13
14   // Use %.4lf for 4 digits of double variable
15   printf("%.4lf", PI);
16
17   return 0;
18}
```

Output

```text
3.141500 3.1415
```
